costa-encandela.pitch: The storybook park, where the lighthouse has been lit every night since 1996.
description: Costa Encandela is the original Isla Velaluz park and still the heart of the island. It was built around El Faro, the lighthouse at the end of the entrance plaza, and everything else grew outward from there: a village of folk tales, a forest that glows after dark, a mermaid bay and an old port town.

It is the gentlest of the three parks. Most rides have no height requirement, a good share of them are indoors, and the day is paced for families who would sooner wander than queue. Come back to the plaza at dusk, when the lanterns go on one string at a time.

punta-tormenta.pitch: The thrill park on the windward point, built for coasters, drops and weather.
description: Punta Tormenta opened in 2004 on the exposed end of the island, and it leans into the setting. The lands are a storm-watch pier, a shipyard, a whirlpool cove, a ridge of towers and, since 2021, a research outpost at the edge of a storm.

This is where the big rides are. Most have a height requirement and nearly all of them are outdoors, which means the park is at the mercy of the sky on summer afternoons. Ride the coasters early, and save the indoor rides and the shows for when the clouds build.

playa-zambulla.pitch: The water park: a wave bay, a lazy river, two slide complexes and a cove for small swimmers.
description: Playa Zambulla opened in 2009 and takes its name from the Spanish for diving in. It is the smallest of the three parks and the easiest to do in a day. Most families claim chairs on Tortuga Beach and work outward from there.
The park keeps shorter hours than the theme parks and closes for part of the winter and on cold days. Check the calendar before you plan around it.
